The presenter quotes 60 to 80 Nm for the flange nuts at the exhaust manifold. That is wrong for those nuts: Jaguar gives 14-18 Nm on a 4.0, and our job follows that. 60-80 Nm is the Torca clamp figure.
The presenter quotes 8 to 12 Nm for the housing bolts. Jaguar gives no figure for these bolts on a 4.0, and 10 Nm is the 4.2 figure. They say you also need their radiator videos for the full job.

The presenter removes the rear anti-roll bar for access and extracts the oil with a shop vac. Our steps use a hand pump and leave the bar on. Check the oil in the video against ours: Shell Spirax Super TS 90.
The presenter replaces the sensor, not cleans it. Our job tries cleaning first.

The presenter runs through the gears with the car raised. Our job keeps it on the ground or a level drive-on ramp for this. They also quote 11 Nm for the pan and about 5.5 Nm for the filter: use the figures in our job.
The presenter says they may not be doing it right. Use the sill jacking plates from our job for the stands.

The presenter says to switch the Jaguar off before taking the leads off if you can. Our job follows the handbook: idle five minutes, then remove them. Both keep the donor engine off. Follow our connection order.

The presenter says to torque to 80 pounds without saying clearly which bolts. If they mean the carrier bolts, about 108 Nm is below our 120-180 Nm, so use ours. They suggest using a torch on rusted bolts: heat near brake parts is a fire risk. They also mention bleeding when they only pump the pedal.

The presenter sprays silicone on the piston and rubber hoses and rests the caliper on the suspension arm. Our steps use neither spray nor that method: keep lube off the pads and disc, and never let the caliper hang on its hose.
The presenter starts on the belt and never mentions the battery. Disconnect it first, as the alternator cable is live. They only show removal.

The presenter supports the car on wooden blocks. Use axle stands as in our job. They drop the pressure by pulling the pump fuse. Our job releases it at the rail valve. Fuel is a fire risk, so work outdoors.

The presenter takes the bonnet struts off and rests the bonnet at 90 degrees on bolts they added. That is a heavy panel, so have a helper. They never mention disconnecting the battery: follow our first step.

The presenter takes the throttle body right off. Our job cleans it in place, which is less risky. Removal also disturbs the coolant hoses and gasket. The chapters show the presenter still diagnosing at the end.
The presenter takes the whole crossbeam off, a much bigger job than our steps. They hold it on a motorcycle stand: use a jack with a wood block as in our job.
The presenter takes the whole housing out, which is more work than our steps need.

The presenter tightens the tower bolts to about 13 Nm. Jaguar gives no figure for these bolts on a 4.0, and 10 Nm is the 4.2 figure. Manifold lifting is an owner method and is not in our job.

The presenter turns the ABS ring off with a blunt chisel and says a breakage there will not matter. Our job uses the proper socket and refits the rotor nut at 270-330 Nm.
